problems.stem: A capstone talk is outlined as: 'Slide 1 home screen, slide 2 menu, slide 3 quiz, slide 4 results.' Why is this a weak presentation narrative?
options: It is a feature tour: the order is driven by the interface, not by a problem-decision-evidence argument.
It should start with the results.
Screenshots are not allowed in a defense.
problems.explanation: A defense narrative is an argument from problem to decisions to evidence, not a walkthrough of screens in interface order.

problems.stem: A presenter's slides are full paragraphs that they read aloud word for word. Which principle does this violate, and what is the fix?
options: The coherence principle; add more decorative images.
The redundancy principle; let slides carry the visual evidence while the spoken narrative carries the argument.
The signaling principle; remove all slide headings.
No principle; reading slides is standard practice.
problems.explanation: Identical text on slides and in speech is redundant and overloads the audience; the spoken and visual channels should carry different loads.

problems.stem: An AI drafts your full talk and includes the line 'usability testing with 30 users confirmed the design.' You only ran 3 informal tryouts. What is the correct response?
options: Keep the line; it sounds stronger and the committee will not check.
Correct the claim to match what your project actually did, then rehearse so you can defend the real evidence.
Run 30 tests the night before to make the line true.
Remove all evidence claims to be safe.
problems.explanation: AI may outline the arc, but every claim must match the real project and be defensible under follow-up questions; reciting unverified claims collapses at the defense.

problems.stem: Your narrative states 'learners found the module engaging.' A committee member asks how you know. What should the narrative have included alongside that claim?
options: A more enthusiastic tone of voice.
An evidence beat for the claim, such as a tryout observation, completion data, or learner comment the committee can probe.
A longer description of the feature.
A statement that engagement is hard to measure.
problems.explanation: Each effectiveness claim needs a paired evidence beat (tryout, data, or theory link) so the committee can interrogate the basis for it.
